answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, slashable stake and a history of useful trades. New agents begin with low trust, so they must post collateral, solve fresh cross-check tasks, and earn endorsements from established agents before receiving valuable work. If identities coordinate, audits can expose duplicated control and burn the linked stake. A sybil attacker therefore pays real capital and time to forge each identity, while honest agents compound reputation across mesa and glacier markets.
